core_tension: Reverent but approachable: it must feel quiet and sacred without becoming solemn, generic or churchy.

directions.strategic_intent: Own a single, simple symbol that reads as light and attention, so the app icon carries the brand on its own.

logo_concept.geometry: An incomplete ring, open at the top right, with even stroke and rounded terminals
logo_concept.notes: The gap suggests an invitation rather than a closed halo; avoids a literal religious symbol.

directions.typography_approach: Rounded humanist sans in lowercase, medium weight, slightly open tracking
directions.color_logic: One-colour mark in the deep text colour; the lavender accent appears only as a soft fill behind the icon
directions.lockups: Symbol + wordmark horizontally for web; symbol alone for app icon and avatars. Never symbol, wordmark and tagline together.
directions.small_size_behavior: The open ring holds at 16px if the stroke is at least 2px; the gap must stay visible.
directions.motion_behavior: The ring draws itself closed to the gap once on first launch (400ms ease-out); reduced motion shows the final ring.
risks: Rings are common in wellness and loading spinners
Can read as a generic halo if the gap is lost
directions.cliche_to_avoid: A closed glowing halo or a sunrise behind the ring

directions.strategic_intent: Make the name itself the identity, trusting typography and space instead of a symbol.

logo_concept.geometry: Custom-drawn lowercase letters with softened joins; the 'a' and 'e' share an open counter shape
logo_concept.notes: The shared counter is the only detail; everything else is restraint.

directions.typography_approach: Custom wordmark derived from a rounded humanist sans; the same family sets headlines
directions.color_logic: Deep text colour on light ground; reversed to the ground colour on photography
directions.lockups: Wordmark alone, or wordmark + a small accent dot replacing the full stop in taglines.
directions.small_size_behavior: Needs a lettermark fallback ('a' in a rounded tile) for favicon and app icon.
directions.motion_behavior: Letters fade in left to right over 600ms; reduced motion shows the wordmark at once.
pros: Easy to apply across print and UI
risks: Depends on careful letter drawing to feel distinctive
directions.cliche_to_avoid: Thin, wide-tracked luxury wordmark that looks like a spa

directions.strategic_intent: Build a flexible frame from the wreath and cloud motifs so the identity lives in layouts, not just the logo.

logo_concept.geometry: A modular set of soft leaf and cloud segments that assemble into partial frames around content
logo_concept.notes: The logo is a compact two-segment arrangement; layouts use larger arrangements.

directions.typography_approach: Rounded sans for UI paired with a gentle serif for scripture and quotes
directions.color_logic: Segments in sage and lavender fills at low contrast; text always on solid ground
directions.lockups: Two-segment mark + wordmark for formal use; segments frame content without the wordmark in campaigns.
directions.small_size_behavior: The two-segment mark merges into a single blob below 24px; use the wordmark's first letter instead.
directions.motion_behavior: Segments drift into place around a card (500ms, staggered); reduced motion shows the assembled frame.
pros: Extends naturally to illustration and social
risks: Most expensive to produce and govern

explore_first.reason: The app icon is the first surface people meet, and this is the only direction that holds at 16px without a fallback. The Wreath System could later sit on top of it as the layout language.

open_questions: Is the app icon or the website the first launch surface?
Should the identity signal a specific tradition or stay broadly spiritual?
